author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: Token-budget gate corpus is unrepresentative in both scale and coverage: budgets are set on a seeded micro-workspace and the largest agent-facing payloads are not measured at all

The shipped token-budget gate (scripts/release/token-budget-gate.mjs over token-budgets.json, delivered under the closed pm-cu1i) passes 14 surfaces green, but its corpus cannot detect the growth it exists to prevent.

Scale. Budgets are measured against an isolated PM_PATH with deterministic seeded items, as the fixture field in token-budgets.json states. Real output on the repository tracker (2,028 items, 2026.7.25) exceeds those ceilings by an order of magnitude:

  next --limit 5      declared max 1,043 B   measured 11,099 B  (~2,774 tokens)
  context --limit 10  declared max 1,098 B   measured  7,214 B  (~1,803 tokens)
  list --status open --limit 20                measured  3,988 B
  get pm-doxj                                  measured 20,290 B (~5,072 tokens)

The ceilings therefore bound a fixture, not a product. A change that doubles per-row cost at real scale keeps the gate green.

Coverage. The two largest agent-facing payloads are absent from the corpus entirely:

  MCP tools/list handshake   38,496 B  ~9,624 tokens  (31 tools)
  aggregate per-command help 187,363 B ~46,841 tokens (76 commands)
  root help                   12,281 B  ~3,070 tokens

The handshake is the largest unavoidable fixed cost: every MCP-connected agent pays it once per session before any work. It has demonstrably grown while the gate stayed green - the pm-a22j baseline recorded 28 tools at 32,979 B (~8.2k tokens) and it is now 31 tools at 38,496 B (~9,624 tokens), a 17 percent increase with no gate that fires. scripts/measure-agent-token-surface.mjs already produces every one of these numbers; nothing consumes them as a ratchet.

Two consequences follow. The gate reports a guarantee it does not provide, and the surface-growth ratchets that pm-wt43zj and pm-kxci8x depend on have no measured cost axis to enforce. pm-5t33or replaces hand-maintained ceilings with contract-declared per-command budgets and is the destination for the declarations; this item owns making the corpus and its fixtures representative so any declaration is enforced against numbers agents actually pay. pm-8pnj measures tokens per completed task end to end and consumes this as its per-surface floor.

Budgets are measured against fixtures at declared scale tiers including at least one workspace of repository size or larger, and each budget records the tier it was measured at, so a ceiling can no longer be set on a micro-workspace and read as a product guarantee; The corpus covers the MCP tools/list handshake payload and the aggregate per-command help surface, sourced from the same measurement the gate uses, so both have ceilings that fail on growth; The gate consumes scripts/measure-agent-token-surface.mjs rather than duplicating measurement, and a single command reproduces every published figure; A coverage assertion fails when a command, MCP tool, or output format exists with no budget entry, so new surfaces cannot be added outside the corpus; The gate reports the delta against the recorded baseline, not only pass or fail, so a change that consumes headroom without breaching is visible in review; The current 31-tool handshake and 76-command help surface are recorded as the new baseline with their measurement method, superseding the stale pm-a22j 28-tool figure wherever it is cited

value.text: Corpus-gap evidence 2026-07-26 (audit plan pm-t9e3bc): in this extension-loaded dogfood workspace the agent-facing payloads exceed every gated fixture budget — pm --help renders 13,398 bytes vs the 11,688-byte fixture budget (7 loaded extensions contribute 21 command handlers the fixture never sees), and contracts --flags-only measures 117,070 bytes vs the 116,189-byte fixture budget. Both gates are green because the fixture is extension-free and micro-scale; the real workspace an agent actually reads is already over budget on both surfaces. Confirms this item's thesis from the agent side: the largest payloads (extension-loaded help/contracts) are the unmeasured ones.
